THE TICKET — SFCC-731 "pdp/gallery", status Code Review, assignee Tim Lavelle, reporter Jasmijn Tsang.

Free-text description (this is now STALE on one point, see below): "As a Developer, I want a reusable pdp/gallery React component built to the Zimmermann Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by pdp/hero to render the product image and video gallery on the PDP. The component renders a sequence of media items (photo and video) in a stacked layout on desktop and a swipeable carousel on mobile. The desktop layout adapts based on total media count. Video is treated as a standard media item and slots into the layout based on its position in the product's media array. The component renders a View Gallery button as a trigger only — the gallery overlay is a separate component and out of scope for this story."

Acceptance Criteria (custom field, edited by Jasmijn Tsang the SAME day as the description above but chronologically AFTER it — this is the authoritative, current scope statement; it directly contradicts the description's last sentence by including the overlay. Treat the AC list as the real scope, not the description):

Default state — desktop layout
1. 3 media items → 3 full-width stacked + View Gallery button
2. 4 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery button
3. 5 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery +1 button
4. 6 media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery button
5. 7+ media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery +X button (X = total minus 6)
6. Video items slot into the layout based on their position in the media array and are not treated differently to photo items for layout purposes.

showGalleryButton prop
7. Given showGalleryButton is false, then no View Gallery button renders regardless of media count.
8. Given showGalleryButton is true, then the View Gallery button renders per the layout thresholds above and is visible and tappable.

Default state — mobile
9. Given the component renders on mobile, then all media items display in a swipeable single-image carousel with a dot indicator bar regardless of media count.
10. Given a shopper swipes, then the active dot indicator updates to reflect the current position.
11. Given showGalleryButton is true on mobile, then the View Gallery button is visible and tappable.

Expanded state — overlay shell
12. Given the View Gallery button is activated, then the gallery opens full-screen taking over the entire viewport.
13. Given the gallery is open, then clicking the close icon dismisses the overlay and returns the shopper to their previous scroll position on the PDP.

Expanded state — gallery header (desktop)
14. Given the gallery is open on desktop, then a sticky header is visible at the top of the overlay containing: product name, active colour name, close icon, and model avatar thumbnails.
15. Given the product has multiple colour variants, then the header includes a colour selector.
16. Given a shopper clicks a model avatar thumbnail, then the gallery scrolls to the corresponding image set for that model.

Expanded state — gallery header (mobile)
17. Given the gallery is open on mobile, then a sticky header is visible containing: product name, close icon, and colour selector. Model avatar thumbnails are not shown on mobile.

Expanded state — image content
18. Given the gallery is open, then the full media array renders as a vertically scrollable stack of full-width media items.
19. Given the gallery renders, then images are served in an optimised format at the appropriate resolution per breakpoint.

Empty & error states
20. Given no media items exist for the product, then the component does not render and no broken layout is shown.
21. Given an image fails to load, then the surrounding layout is maintained without a broken image rendering.

Accessibility
22. Given the gallery overlay opens, then focus moves into it and is trapped within until closed.
23. Given the gallery overlay closes, then focus returns to the View Gallery button that triggered it.
24. The overlay has role=dialog and an appropriate aria-label.
25. The component meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

CROSS-TICKET CONTEXT (for your scope judgment only, not something to resolve):
- SFCC-186 "PDP – Product Image Gallery" (assignee: also Tim Lavelle, status: also Code Review) is a separate, higher-level ticket that "blocks" SFCC-731 and covers the base image-gallery shopper story (no video). It's plausible this same PR or a tightly-linked one is intended to close SFCC-186 too — check whether the PR's delivered functionality actually covers SFCC-186's description ("PDP displays a product image gallery... images managed at colour-variation level... switching colour updates gallery without full page reload... stacked editorial layout desktop, swipeable carousel mobile... primary hero priority-loaded... consistent aspect ratio... video out of scope, see SFCC-188").
- SFCC-187 "PDP – Image Gallery Open State" (assignee: Jasmijn Tsang, status: Blocked) is a separate ticket whose description is exactly the overlay/expanded-state functionality (ACs 12-25 above look like they were lifted directly from what SFCC-187 would have specified). It "blocks" SFCC-731. Note whether this PR's overlay work looks like it fully satisfies what SFCC-187 would need — this matters for the scope verdict (is the overlay "in scope" because SFCC-731's own ACs say so, which is settled — yes it's in scope for 731 — but is it *complete* against what a shopper-facing overlay story would need, e.g. do NOT assume SFCC-187 is irrelevant just because it's a different ticket number).
- SFCC-188 "PDP – Product Video in Gallery" is Blocked, video data source doesn't exist yet. The PR's own commits say video renders as "a positional slot only." Confirm this matches AC 6 (video slots into position, not treated differently for layout) without overclaiming actual video playback functionality.

YOUR TASK:
1. Go through all 25 ACs against the actual diff/code in the head worktree (not just the PR description's claims — verify in the source). For each AC: met / partially met / not met / not verifiable from code alone (needs live browser check — flag these for the human reviewer instead of guessing).
2. Flag anything the PR does that ISN'T traceable to one of the 25 ACs or to a clearly-necessary supporting change (e.g., activating PageContainer for full-bleed layout, or the ZimmButton sx prop needed to style the gallery's own button, are supporting/necessary — but flag anything that looks like unrelated scope creep beyond that).
3. Give your scope verdict: under-delivered (name the missing ACs), over-delivered (name the excess), or on-scope. Pay particular attention to AC 16 (model avatar thumbnails) — the PR's commit messages never mention this feature at all, only a colour-swatch row; determine from the actual overlay component code whether AC 16 is implemented, silently dropped, or was never applicable (e.g., if "model avatar thumbnails" require multi-model photography data that doesn't exist yet — check if there's any such data source referenced anywhere in the product/media types this PR consumes).
4. Report concisely: a verdict line, then the AC-by-AC table, then any scope-creep or gap flags with file:line.

13	 * resizing is meaningless for a URL that already *is* the image bytes (there's no server to ask),

24	  if (url.startsWith('data:') || url.startsWith('blob:')) return url;

# Scope Conformance Review — PR #81 (SFCC-731 "pdp/gallery")

## Verdict

**UNDER-DELIVERED on one AC (AC 16), PARTIALLY on two others (AC 14, AC 19) — everything else in the 25-AC list is met or reasonably interpreted. No over-delivery beyond necessary supporting changes.** The gap is not a build failure — it's a **silent substitution**: the PR builds a generic per-image "jump to photo N" thumbnail strip, then labels it (in test/story comments only, never in a commit message or code comment) as satisfying AC 16 ("model avatar thumbnails... scrolls to the corresponding image set for that model"), a materially different feature that no data source in this codebase currently supports. This should have been surfaced as a flagged gap (the way the video/SFCC-188 gap and the two provisional pixel-value gaps *are* explicitly flagged elsewhere in this same PR) rather than quietly relabeled as done.

## AC 16 deep-dive (as requested)

**Finding: AC 16 was silently reinterpreted, not implemented, and not disclosed as a gap.**

What's built: `thumbnailStrip` in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:229-256` — one thumbnail **per media item** (`media.map`), 102×136px, same 3:4 `GALLERY_ITEM_ASPECT_RATIO` every other gallery tile uses (`zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts:96-115`), each labelled `"Go to image {i} of {total}"` and clicking calls `scrollToItem(i)` — a 1:1 jump-to-single-image control, not a per-model grouping.

What AC 16 asks for: "clicks a **model avatar** thumbnail... scrolls to the corresponding **image set for that model**" — this requires (a) knowing which images belong to which model, and (b) an avatar-style UI distinct from the per-photo thumbnail. Neither exists:
- `ZimmGalleryMediaItem` (`zimmMediaTile/index.tsx:21-40`) has only `kind`/`src`/`alt`/`posterSrc`/`posterAlt` — no model identifier.
- `mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.ts:13-27` maps straight from SFCC's `ImageGroup` (`images`, `variationAttributes`, `viewType` — confirmed against `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own type, no model field) — nothing to group by.
- Repo-wide grep for `avatar` (`.ts`/`.tsx`, `.docs/`) returns **zero** hits. `.docs/prd/pdp.md:175` lists "model shots" only as one of several photo *types* (front/back/detail/model), not a grouping/navigation concept.

Yet the substitution is explicitly labeled as satisfying the AC: the test file's own `describe` block is titled `'ZimmGalleryOverlay — thumbnail strip (AC 14/16)'` (`zimmGalleryOverlay/index.test.tsx:100`), and the story has `/** AC 16 — clicking a thumbnail scrolls the stack to that image. */` (`zimmGalleryOverlay/index.stories.tsx:95`). Contrast this with how the *other* known gap in this same PR was handled: the video item's lack of real playback data is disclosed openly, in-code, three separate times (`zimmMediaTile/index.tsx:29-38`, `mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.ts:8-11`, PR body: "Video renders as a positional slot only... SFCC-188 is blocked"). AC 16 got no equivalent disclosure anywhere — not in a code comment, not in the PR body, not in a "Known gaps" note.

Given no model-grouping data source exists anywhere the PR touches, literal AC 16 probably isn't buildable yet — that's a legitimate reason to substitute. But the correct move (per this repo's own established pattern, and per AGENTS.md's "ambiguous/unconfirmed requirement → stop, flag, propose" rule) was to flag it to Jasmijn as a gap against SFCC-187's presumed future spec, not to quietly ship a different feature under the same AC number.
